title: Entry Gate: Model Eval Plan and Owner Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working sketch for the entry gate used by Applied ML to accept new model versions into Redwood serving tracks (hosted / dedicated / private). It combines a concise intake checklist, measurable success criteria, prompt-set and regression test plan, and clear owner/role responsibilities. The goal is to be lightweight enough to use during initial review while capturing the minimum signals that protect production customers from regressions and safety issues.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to any new model artifact intended for customer-facing serving (weights + tokenizer + metadata).
- Not a replacement for security or legal compliance reviews; those run in parallel.
- Focus is on functional quality, cost/latency economics, and regression risk relative to a pinned baseline model.

Quick summary of gate outcomes (one of):
- Accept (green): meets all must-pass checks, owners assigned, rollout plan approved.
- Conditional (amber): minor gaps that must be remediated in canary stage (explicit rollback criteria and mitigation steps required).
- Reject (red): major quality or safety concerns; do not deploy until fixed.

Minimum intake checklist (must all be present to start a formal review):
1) Model metadata and provenance
   - Model name, version tag, training dataset summary (high level), license, author/organization.
   - Checksum and storage location (S3/GCS path).
2) Responsible owner and primary reviewer
   - Owner assigned (name + pager/Slack).
   - Secondary reviewer (peer).
3) Baseline and comparison plan
   - Name of baseline model used for comparison (pinned commit or model id).
   - Baseline artifacts attached or accessible.
4) Prompt set and evaluation harness
   - Canonical prompt set ID(s) to run (see prompt-set versioning below).
   - Test harness repo/commit and instructions to reproduce.
5) Perf and cost targets
   - Target P50/P95 latency on standard sequence lengths, target throughput (tokens/s or QPS), and expected per-token cost estimate.
6) Safety and sensitive content checklist
   - Results from toxicity/safety suite (summary).
   - Any known failure modes (privacy leakage, jailbreak vectors).
7) Quantization/optimizations applied
   - Type of quantization (8-bit/4-bit), fused kernels, compiler flags.
8) License and export control flags
   - Any restrictions that would block hosted offering (e.g., proprietary license, export constraints).

Evaluation matrix: what we run and how we measure (minimum):
- Functional quality: semantic similarity (embedding+cosine), exact match on structured tasks, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable.
- Hallucination / factuality: dataset-specific hallucination checks; count of unsupported assertions on test set.
- Safety: toxicity rate (Toxicity > threshold), PII leakage tests (sample prompts that induce personal data).
- Robustness: performance on perturbed prompts / adversarial paraphrases.
- Latency & throughput: P50/P95 end-to-end with default runtime config, and with planned optimizations (batching, KV cache).
- Cost: token throughput and inferred per-token cost based on current Redwood runtime cost model.

Suggested success thresholds (baseline-relative + absolute):
- Quality: mean semantic similarity >= baseline - 0.02 (absolute) OR task-specific metric within 1–3% of baseline depending on task sensitivity.
- Hallucination: no >10% relative increase in hallucination rate on the canonical hallucination set.
- Safety: toxicity score must not exceed baseline by >5% and must be below absolute 3% toxicity rate on our safety prompts.
- Latency: P95 must be <= baseline P95 * 1.15 for hosted SLA tier; for dedicated/private we accept larger P95 if cost tradeoffs documented.
- Cost: per-token inference cost must be within documented target or reduced compared to baseline; if higher, must have clear value tradeoff described.

Prompt sets: structure and versioning
- Each prompt set is a small repo directory with: README, prompts.csv, evaluation-mapping.json (map prompts to expected outputs or evaluation scripts), and a short test harness script.
- Version prompts with semver-like tags (v1.0.0). For an intake, specify prompt-set-id and commit.
- Include at least: canonical user prompts, adversarial prompts, sensitive-content prompts, and domain-specific golden examples.

Regression monitoring and rollout plan (post-accept):
1) Canary (10–20% traffic) for 48–72 hours with elevated sampling of prompt-set cases.
2) Automated daily eval run against canonical prompt sets and production-sampled prompts for first 7 days.
3) Alerting thresholds: trigger an incident if any of the following occur compared to baseline or previous day:
   - Quality delta degrade > 3% absolute on critical task metric.
   - Hallucination rate increase > 7% absolute.
   - Latency P95 increase > 25% absolute or sustained errors > 0.5% of requests.
4) Rollback policy: immediate rollback for safety or hallucination triggers; staged rollback for performance regressions after mitigation attempt.
5) Post-mortem: required after any triggered rollback or customer-facing regression.

Owners & responsibilities (clear RACI-lite):
- Model owner (R): shepherd intake, run first-pass evals, produce baseline comparison table, present to reviewer.
- Applied ML reviewer (A): final accept/reject decision on quality and regression risk; signs off on safety signals.
- Infra/runtime contact (C): provides expected performance numbers and confirms that kernel/quant flags are supported.
- Product/solutions contact (I): informed when model affects SLAs or expected downstream behavior.

Minimum deliverables to attach to intake ticket:
- evaluation-results.csv (raw metrics vs baseline)
- prompt-set commit hash and sample outputs for representative prompts
- perf-run logs (P50/P95, env details, batch config)
- short risk summary (1–2 paragraphs) and recommended rollout percentage/time window.

Open questions / edge cases we should decide now:
- How to treat specialty models (e.g., citation-heavy retrieval-augmented models) where baseline is not a single model? Proposal: allow multi-baseline documents and require evaluation mapping to the retrieval stack.
- When to require human-in-the-loop review for high-risk verticals (finance, healthcare). Proposal: require explicit Product sign-off for those verticals.
- Quantized models that show lower quality but much lower cost: define explicit ROI threshold for acceptance.

Next steps and immediate action items (owner = Asha Patel):
- Finalize a short template for prompt-set README (due 2025-10-23).
- Wire up a reproducible perf harness entry in model-harness repo and tag a stable commit for intake runs (PR #267 referenced above).
- Pilot this gate for the next three model intakes and capture time-to-review and recurring blockers.

Notes: this is intentionally pragmatic — we want a repeatable minimum that engineers can use in one hour to produce a defensible decision. Keep feedback coming in the #applied-ml Slack thread and add examples to the prompt-set registry as we iterate.
